title: The Ethics of Collecting and Using Information: A Community Archive Project
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何官方分数。请先听/读英文转录稿，完成10道听力/阅读题（含单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。然后学习语法讲解（叙事时态、描述从句、原因与例子；减少反复出现的基础错误），完成8道新句语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文；解释为中文。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
transcript:
Maya: Hi, Daniel. You look busy. What are you working on?
Daniel: I'm helping the Riverside Community Archive. We collect old photos and letters from local families. Then we put them online.
Maya: That sounds nice. But I have a question. Do you ask people before you put their family photos online?
Daniel: Yes, we do. We always ask for written permission. Last month, a woman named Mrs. Chen gave us a box of letters. She signed a form, and she chose which letters we could share.
Maya: Good. But what about people in the photos? Maybe they didn't agree.
Daniel: That's a real problem. We learned that lesson last year. We uploaded a photo of a school class from 1965. One man in the photo called us. He was angry because he didn't want his childhood picture on the internet. We took the photo down the same day.
Maya: So what is your rule now?
Daniel: Now we have three rules. First, we ask the person who owns the item. Second, if the photo shows living people, we try to contact them. Third, if someone says no, we don't share it. We keep it in the archive building, but not online.
Maya: That sounds fair. But contacting everyone sounds hard.
Daniel: It is hard. Sometimes we can't find people. Then we don't publish the photo. We only publish photos of people who have agreed, or photos where everyone in the picture is no longer living.
Maya: Wait, is that last rule okay? Some families might still care.
Daniel: You're right. We changed that rule too. Now, even for old photos, we ask the family if we can find them. If we can't find the family, we wait.
Maya: I see. What about information like addresses or phone numbers in old letters?
Daniel: We remove private details. For example, last week I read a letter from 1972. It had a home address and a phone number. I blacked them out before we put the letter online. The letter is still useful for history, but the private information is hidden.
Maya: That's a good example. Do you also collect information from social media?
Daniel: No, we don't. We only use things that people give us directly. We don't copy posts from Facebook or WeChat. That would be wrong because people didn't give us permission.
Maya: What if a person gives you information, but later they change their mind?
Daniel: Then we remove it. Last spring, a man named Mr. Patel shared a recording of his father's stories. Two months later, he asked us to delete it. We deleted it immediately. We didn't argue.
Maya: That's respectful. How do you explain your rules to the public?
Daniel: We have a short page on our website. It says: 'We ask first. We protect private details. We remove things when people ask.' We also give talks at the library. Next month, I'm giving a talk about why consent matters.
Maya: I'd like to come. Can I bring my students?
Daniel: Of course. The talk is on Saturday at 2 p.m. It's free. But please tell me how many students are coming, because the room is small.
Maya: I will. Thanks, Daniel. This conversation made me think about my own photos.
Daniel: Me too. Actually, after our talk last year, I deleted some old photos of my friends from my phone. I didn't ask them before I posted those pictures. I felt bad.
Maya: That's honest. So the rules are not just for the archive.
Daniel: Right. They are for everyone who collects and shares information.

options: Old photos and letters
Newspapers and magazines
School books and toys
Maps and tickets

questions.prompt: What did Mrs. Chen do before the archive shared her letters?
options: She signed a form and chose letters.
She called the archive and complained.
She deleted her social media posts.
She gave a talk at the library.
answers: She signed a form and chose letters.

options: A man in the photo did not want it online.
The photo was too old to see.
The school asked for money.
The photo had no permission form.

questions.explanation: 原文说 'He was angry because he didn't want his childhood picture on the internet. We took the photo down the same day.' 因此是因为照片中的一位男士不希望照片上网。

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the transcript: Daniel says they remove private ______ from old letters.

options: He blacks them out.
He writes them in a new letter.
He gives them to the police.
He puts them on Facebook.

questions.evidence: I blacked them out before we put the letter online.

questions.prompt: Which heading best matches Daniel's rule about social media?

Collecting posts from WeChat
Sharing posts with friends
Deleting all social media

questions.evidence: We don't copy posts from Facebook or WeChat. That would be wrong because people didn't give us permission.

They asked him to pay a fee.
They posted it on the website.
They lost the recording.

questions.evidence: The talk is on Saturday at 2 p.m. It's free.

grammar.title: 叙事时态、描述从句、原因与例子；减少反复出现的基础错误
grammar.explanation: 在讲述过去发生的事情时，主句用一般过去时（如 uploaded, called, took），表示先后顺序；描述人或物时，用描述从句（who/that/which）把信息放在名词后面，例如 'a man who was angry'；说明原因时用 because，举例时用 for example 或 such as。常见基础错误包括：主语和动词不一致（he don't → he doesn't）、时态混用（Last year we upload → Last year we uploaded）、以及 because 后接不完整句子。请先理解意思，再记术语。
grammar.example: One man in the photo called us. He was angry because he didn't want his childhood picture on the internet.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about a past event.
options: Last week, she shared a photo and asked her friends first.
Last week, she share a photo and ask her friends first.
Last week, she shares a photo and asks her friends first.
Last week, she sharing a photo and asking her friends first.
answers: Last week, she shared a photo and asked her friends first.
questions.explanation: Last week 表示过去，主句动词用一般过去时 shared 和 asked。其他选项时态或主谓一致错误。
questions.evidence: We uploaded a photo of a school class from 1965.

options: The woman who signed the form is my neighbor.
The woman which signed the form is my neighbor.
The woman who signed the form are my neighbor.
The woman signed the form who is my neighbor.
answers: The woman who signed the form is my neighbor.
questions.explanation: 描述人用 who；主语 The woman 是单数，谓语用 is。which 不用于人，are 与单数主语不一致。
questions.evidence: We always ask for written permission.

options: He deleted the post because he didn't want it online.
He deleted the post because he don't want it online.
He deleted the post because he not want it online.
He deleted the post because he didn't wanted it online.
answers: He deleted the post because he didn't want it online.
questions.explanation: because 后接完整从句；didn't 后接动词原形 want。don't 与 he 不一致，not want 缺少助动词，didn't wanted 形式错误。
questions.evidence: He was angry because he didn't want his childhood picture on the internet.

options: We hide private details, for example, phone numbers.
We hide private details, for example, phone numbers are hidden.
We hide private details, for example, because phone numbers.
We hide private details, for example, phone numbers hides.
answers: We hide private details, for example, phone numbers.
questions.explanation: for example 后接名词或名词短语举例，phone numbers 是 private details 的例子。其他选项结构不完整或主谓不一致。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past narrative sentence.
options: Two months later, he asked us to delete it, and we deleted it immediately.
Two months later, he asks us to delete it, and we delete it immediately.
Two months later, he asked us to delete it, and we delete it immediately.
Two months later, he asking us to delete it, and we deleted it immediately.
answers: Two months later, he asked us to delete it, and we deleted it immediately.
questions.explanation: Two months later 表示过去，两个动作都用一般过去时 asked 和 deleted，保持叙事时态一致。
questions.evidence: Two months later, he asked us to delete it. We deleted it immediately.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct description clause for a thing.
options: The letter that has a home address is private.
The letter who has a home address is private.
The letter that have a home address is private.
The letter has a home address that is private letter.
answers: The letter that has a home address is private.
questions.explanation: 描述事物用 that；The letter 是单数，从句谓语用 has。who 用于人，have 与单数主语不一致。
questions.evidence: It had a home address and a phone number.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with such as.
options: We collect family items such as letters and photos.
We collect family items such as letters and photos are old.
We collect family items such as because letters and photos.
We collect family items such as letters and photos collects.
answers: We collect family items such as letters and photos.
questions.explanation: such as 后接名词短语举例，letters and photos 是 family items 的例子。其他选项结构错误。
questions.evidence: We collect old photos and letters from local families.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with a past passive.
options: The photo was taken down the same day.
The photo were taken down the same day.
The photo was took down the same day.
The photo taken down the same day.
answers: The photo was taken down the same day.
questions.explanation: 被动语态用 be + 过去分词；The photo 是单数，用 was，take 的过去分词是 taken。
questions.evidence: We took the photo down the same day.

part1: Do you often take photos of other people?
Do you ask before you share a photo online?
What kind of information do you keep private?
Have you ever deleted a post or a photo? Why?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you had to decide whether to share someone's information. You should say: what the information was; who it belonged to; why you needed to decide; and explain what you did and why.
part3: Why is it important to ask for permission before sharing information?
How can people protect private details in old letters or photos?
Should schools teach students about online privacy? Why or why not?
What problems can happen when people share information without consent?

transfer.writing: Write a short email (120–150 words) to a local history club. Explain that you want to share an old family photo online, describe one private detail in the photo, and ask what permission the club needs before publishing it. Give one reason and one example.
